edge-case.def: An input at the boundary of what is allowed (empty list, one item, all equal, negatives, the largest size). Most bugs hide here, so always test them.

big-o.def: A way to say how the number of steps grows with the input size \(n\), ignoring constants and smaller terms: \(3n^2+5n+2=O(n^2)\).

space-complexity.def: How much extra memory an algorithm needs on top of its input, written in Big-O. A few variables: \(O(1)\); a new list as long as the input: \(O(n)\).

two-pointers.def: Two index variables that move through a list (from both ends, or one behind the other) so that one pass solves the problem.

palindrome.def: A sequence that reads the same forwards and backwards, such as level or 12321.

set.def: An unordered collection of distinct items with \(O(1)\) average-time add and in. Made with set() or {1, 2, 3}.
